description: See how choosing between fn.env and env when extending the call environment switches an AST interpreter between lexical and dynamic scoping.
source: draft: agy free model + edit: codex

steps.description: Lines 4-15 define six AST node dataclasses (`Num`, `Var`, `Add`, `Fun`, `Call`, `Let`). `Env.extend(name, value)` (lines 28-29) returns a new child `Env({name: value}, self)`, and `Closure` (lines 32-35) stores `param`, `body`, and `env`.

In `interp(e, env, lexical)`, evaluating `Fun` on line 43 returns `Closure(e.param, e.body, env)` without running `e.body`. When `Call` runs on lines 49-58, line 56 picks `base = fn.env if lexical else env` and evaluates `fn.body` in `base.extend(fn.param, arg)`.

Look at lines 43 and 56 together. Line 43 saves the defining environment in `Closure.env`. Line 56 chooses whether the call body extends saved `fn.env` (`lexical = True`) or the caller's `env` (`lexical = False`).
Lines 63-71 build `program`: `let x = 10 in let f = fun y -> x + y in let x = 99 in f(1)`. They run `interp` with `lexical = True` (`11`) and `lexical = False` (`100`).

steps.answer: When `lexical` is `True`, `bump` uses `n = 1` from `fn.env` on both calls (`0 + 1 + 1`) and returns `2`. When `lexical` is `False`, `bump` uses `n = 500` from the caller's `env` on both calls (`0 + 500 + 500`). It returns `1000`.
steps.question: Consider `program2` on lines 80-83: `let n = 1 in let bump = fun k -> n + k in let n = 500 in bump(bump(0))`. What does `bump(bump(0))` evaluate to when `lexical` is `True` versus when `lexical` is `False`?

steps.description: Lines 80-88 run `program2` under both settings, printing `2` for lexical scope and `1000` for dynamic scope.
At trace step 79 while starting `interp(program, Env(), True)`, line 46 evaluates the outer `Let` binding `x = 10` before extending the environment for `f`.

title: Lexical vs. Dynamic Scope in One Line of an AST Evaluator
